committed_turns.public_event: A newcomer has reached the card room.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: A coin rings off the table edge and wobbles across the floor toward the south door, and nobody at the card table moves to catch it. Four of them sit at a worn table near that door, pale as candle tallow, pointed teeth showing when they breathe, dressed in lace and velvet gone shiny at the elbows. Each has coins stacked in front of them; a silver ring sits among the stacks in the middle. The man dealing has stopped mid-hand, one card pinned between two fingers. Beyond them, the whole north wall is a carved mountain, tiny dwarves in tiny caverns, stone sunbeams fanning over a long tub sunk into the floor.
Narrator: When the dealer speaks it is slow and savoring, each word laid down like a card he means you to look at.
Dealer: Well, now. The door brought us company. Come in, come in, the passage is draftier than we are. That coin by your boot is the most interesting thing that has happened at this table in an hour, so tell me: are you the sort who picks it up, or the sort who waits to see whose it is?

committed_turns.player_input: I sidle up beside the dealer, smile, and say, "Do you always look this dangerous, or is it the candlelight?"
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "I sidle up beside the dealer, smile, and say, "Do you always look this dangerous, or is it the candlelight?""
committed_turns.spoken:
Kit: You walked straight past three sets of fangs to flirt with the fourth. Noted.
Dealer: Candlelight is the kindest friend a face like mine ever had, and I'd hate to disappoint it. Always, I'm afraid. It is exhausting. But a charming thing like you did not come all this way down to compliment a man's complexion. So tell me, while you're standing this close: what do you want that the smile hasn't already got you?
Narrator: He tilts his card so the flame runs along its edge. Across the table, the player by the door rolls his eyes so hard his whole head goes with them.

committed_turns.player_input: I laugh, touch his sleeve, and say, "I don't gamble with money. I gamble with company. Buy me a hand?"
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "I laugh, touch his sleeve, and say, "I don't gamble with money. I gamble with company. Buy me a hand?""
committed_turns.spoken:
Dealer: Company. Now there's a currency nobody down here ever has enough of. All right. I will buy you a hand. If you win, you keep whatever it wins. If you lose, you owe me one small favor, to be named at a time of my choosing. Nothing indecent. Probably. Sit.
Narrator: He hooks the chair beside him with one boot and drags it out. Across the table, the player by the fresco sighs through his teeth and tosses his cards in.
Card player: Deal or don't. Some of us are losing actual money.

appraisal.cause: She asks him to stake her a hand in exchange for her company.

improv_read.connection: He profits from newcomers; staking her costs him nothing with a deck he controls, and the terms let him set a price later. The rest of the table resents losing money to his showing off.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit stays out of it; the flirtation has become a negotiation and the players’ irritation shows the room has its own opinion.

committed_turns.player_input: I sit, lean in close, and say, "Deal. But if I win, you walk me to that door yourself."
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "I sit, lean in close, and say, "Deal. But if I win, you walk me to that door yourself.""
committed_turns.spoken:
Dealer: Walk you to the door. On my arm, I suppose, like a gentleman.
Narrator: For one sentence the drawl drops away and his voice goes short and exact.
Dealer: And if you lose, the door costs what it costs everyone. Ten gold. No favors, no company, coin.
Narrator: Then the warmth is back as if it never left. Two cards whisper across the wood and stop in front of you, face down.
Dealer: There. Now we're both gambling. Look whenever your nerve is ready.

improv_read.connection: She has named passage as her prize, which touches the gang’s real business; he likes the game but restates the true price if she loses, because control of the door is the thing he actually sells.
improv_read.kit_choice: The flirtation has found the room’s real stakes by itself. Kit lets the dealer name them in his crisp voice and stays silent so it lands.
